seed: Shannon Byrne Susko, training of 26-Sep-2026 (individual priorities outside the meeting from the annual); Byron, 17-Nov-2026 (weekly CEO email).

slides.title: What are your annual targets?
slides.support: Take the numbers from the forecast you just agreed. Confirm the fiscal year and its end date.
body: Gross revenue, margin and ending cash.
One widget for each hand-off on your KFFM, plus head count.
Name an owner for every number.
Is each target big enough to keep you on track for your new 3HAG?
notes: The numbers come from the forecast the team just agreed. Confirm them. Do not rebuild them.
The 1HAG is the first year of the new 3HAG. Check each number against the three-year targets the team set yesterday.
slides.headline: What are your annual targets?

slides.title: What must you build this year?
slides.support: Start from your differentiators and the first four quarters of your swim lanes.
body: For each differentiator: what must this year deliver to build it?
Add a priority that moves a KFFM lever if cash needs it.
List every candidate. Then pick ideally 3, up to 5.
Give each an owner, a done-by date, a measure of success and an achieved-by date.
notes: At the Kick Off the team started from its key capabilities. The differentiators have taken their place.
The big moves in the first four quarters of the swim lanes are the natural candidates. Add anything burning on the KFFM.
List every candidate before choosing. Ideally 3, up to 5 priorities for the year, each with one owner, a done-by date and a measure of success.
slides.headline: What must you build this year?

slides.title: Set your own priorities with your own team.
body: Start from the new QHAG and your critical number.
Up to 5 work priorities. Two delivered beat five started.
notes: The team has set individual priorities in the room four times. From the annual on, each leader sets theirs outside the session, with their own team.
A company priority you own goes first and wins if time runs short.
Each leader’s priorities are in Metronome before the first weekly meeting of the quarter.
slides.headline: Set your own priorities with your own team.

slides.title: Is the CEO’s weekly email going out?
slides.support: One page, from the CEO to everyone, by Friday noon.
body: Running: has it gone out every week?
Working: does it carry good news, the numbers and priority status?
What to change? Rate it 0 to 2.
notes: The weekly email started last quarter. Rate it the same way as the meetings: 0 below, 1 meets, 2 exceeds expectations.
Team members send their status to the CEO by Thursday noon.
slides.headline: Is the CEO’s weekly email going out?
